traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Acanthaceae, which takes in Thomandersiaceae: leaves opposite; leaves simple; margins entire, crenate, serrate or dentate; veins pinnate; stipules usually absent, often present; leaf rosettes basal or none; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary, in cymes or in racemes; flowers usually zygomorphic, sometimes actinomorphic; irregular flowers bilabiate; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule; parts of each whorl 4 to 5; stamens 2 to 4 (-5); carpels 2. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
